solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Plant disease bad at first, not serious after

indicators.note: after puts the not-serious word behind the letter taken from bad
at first asks for only the opening letter of the word bad

parts.note: something light is trivial, not serious

explanation.surface: A gardener notes a plant problem that started badly but then eased off.
explanation.definitionFit: Blight is a common name for many fungal diseases that wither crops such as potatoes.

clue.text: Cook hearing donkey calls

indicators.note: hearing says the word is identified by how it sounds when said

parts.note: a donkey's call is a bray, so its calls are brays

explanation.surface: A cook listens to donkeys braying in the yard.
explanation.definitionFit: To braise is a cooking method: brown, then simmer slowly in a little liquid in a covered pot.

clue.text: Terrible input failing: it's possible to be halted

indicators.note: failing suggests the words break down and their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A computer's poor input failing means the program can be stopped midway.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be stopped or broken off midway is capable of interruption.

clue.text: Animal runs into water-pipe

indicators.note: into means the runs letter goes inside the pipe word

parts.note: a hose is a flexible pipe for water
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An animal dashes into a garden hosepipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse is a large domesticated animal, so animal is its general category.

clue.text: Criminal gang with computer technology

parts.note: a band is a group or gang of people
IT is information technology, the computing field

explanation.surface: A crook teams up with a gang and some technical expertise.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit is an outlaw or robber, so a criminal in the noun sense.

clue.text: Took for granted sea's churned with mud

indicators.note: churned means the letters are stirred up into a new order, like sea and mud mixing

explanation.surface: Someone took it for granted that the sea would be churned up with mud.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume something is to suppose it without proof, i.e. take it for granted.

clue.text: Avoiding alcohol is essential for life

definitions.meaning: sipping only something non-alcoholic, as in being on the wagon
something every living thing needs to survive

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is someone choosing water over booze; the second is the potable stuff itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Potable supply from the tap is what humans need to survive, so it is vital for living.

clue.text: Renter leaving article in temporary accommodation

indicators.note: in says the article sits inside the word for temporary accommodation

parts.note: a tent is a temporary shelter
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A renter moving out leaves something in a temporary shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenant occupies property in return for paying rent to a landlord.

clue.text: In search of stylish clothes, in a way

definitions.meaning: read literally, going after something fashionable: chasing a fashion
the idiom meaning to some extent, though not very well

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is cryptic: someone hunting for the latest style is literally pursuing it. The second is the plain idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means somewhat or after a fashion of sorts, i.e. in some manner but not entirely satisfactorily.

clue.text: Lucky having strength to catch big fish

indicators.note: to catch means the strength word holds the fish inside it

parts.note: a forte is a person's strong point or strength
the tuna is a large sea fish

explanation.surface: An angler is lucky to have the strength to land a huge fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortunate is a direct synonym of lucky, blessed by good fortune.

clue.text: Swell of waves certain to involve gallons

indicators.note: to involve means one word takes the other inside it

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: A sailor is sure the swell will be measured in gallons of seawater.
explanation.definitionFit: A surge is a sudden powerful rising of the sea, a heavy swell.

clue.text: With baked cheese dish, stuff European family …

parts.note: to ram is to cram or stuff something in
kin means one's family or relatives

explanation.surface: Read with the next clue, a cook crams a European family with cheesy bakes and heavy puddings.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing dots link this clue's surface to the next one; they play no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramekin is a small baked cheese preparation, and also the little ovenproof pot it is cooked in.

clue.text: … stodge, remarkably undisputed good

indicators.note: remarkably suggests the letters of undisputed are put into a striking new order

explanation.surface: Continuing the family meal: heavy food that is, without question, good.
explanation.definitionFit: Stodge is heavy, filling food, and a steamed pudding made with beef fat is the classic example.

clue.text: Drank a toast initially, drunk in this?

definitions.text: Drank a toast initially, drunk in this?

indicators.note: initially asks for only the opening letter of toast
drunk suggests the letters of drank a are reeling into a new order

explanation.surface: A toast was raised, and the question is what vessel it was drunk from.
explanation.definitionFit: A tankard is a large beer mug, the very thing one might drink a toast from.

clue.text: Gaps in small steps

parts.note: paces are steps

explanation.surface: The gaps in a walkway are just small steps apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaces and gaps are synonyms: empty intervals between things.

clue.text: Crucial moments as cold gets stronger

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a wind or feeling that rises grows stronger

explanation.surface: Critical times arrive as a cold snap intensifies.
explanation.definitionFit: Crises are turning points, decisive times when things could go either way.

clue.text: Flower college planted in a mixture of peat

indicators.note: planted in means the college word is set inside the other letters, like a bulb in soil
a mixture of means the letters of peat are stirred into a new order

parts.note: uni is short for university, a college

explanation.surface: A college gardener plants something in a mix of peat compost.
explanation.definitionFit: The petunia is a popular bedding plant grown for its trumpet-shaped blooms.

clue.text: Garden machinery's method of operation we start to recognise

parts.note: MO stands for modus operandi, Latin for method of operation

indicators.note: start to asks for just the opening letter of recognise

explanation.surface: A manual explains how a piece of garden equipment works, which we begin to understand.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawnmower is a machine for cutting grass, a standard bit of garden equipment.

clue.text: A Muslim leader, I had pork product rejected

indicators.note: rejected means the letters are turned back, read in the opposite direction

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
ham is cured pork

explanation.surface: A Muslim leader declines the pork offered, as Islam forbids it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Islamic belief the Mahdi is a prophesied redeemer and leader; the title was claimed by a Sudanese leader in the 1880s.

clue.text: Some all aflutter in taxi grab English cricket outfit

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
to bag is to seize or grab
whites are the white clothing worn by cricketers

explanation.surface: Some people get flustered trying to grab a taxi in English cricket gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all aflutter' is the definition: the answer is a butterfly, and some of them fluttering are this kind.
explanation.definitionFit: These common white butterflies flutter about gardens, so some fluttering insects are of this species.

clue.text: Ready follower is resolute

definitions.meaning: in the starting call 'Ready, ..., go!' this is the word that comes after ready

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition plays on the race-starting call 'Ready, steady, go'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone firm and unwavering in purpose is described as steady, a synonym of resolute.

clue.text: Fruit used in reversing hives (urticaria)

indicators.note: reversing says the hidden letters are read backwards
used in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A fruit is prescribed as part of a remedy for an itchy skin rash.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Fruit used' as the definition, but 'used' does not define a fruit; 'used in' signals the hidden SURTIC, which 'reversing' turns back.
explanation.definitionFit: Citrus is the family of fruits including oranges, lemons and limes.
